clue.text: Charts showing me origins of shipping forecast areas: peril at sea

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter
letters that are at sea are confused and out of place

blocks.note: first letters of shipping, forecast, areas

explanation.surface: A listener worries about danger at sea while studying the areas of the Shipping Forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shipping Forecast is the Radio 4 weather bulletin for the sea areas around Britain, so 'charts' and 'peril at sea' feel like one picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief maps are charts that show the height and shape of the land.

clue.text: For starters, Roger Allam didn’t attend … ____!

definitions.text: For starters, Roger Allam didn’t attend … ____!

indicators.note: starters are the first letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of Roger, Allam, didn’t, attend

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank fact about the actor Roger Allam's training.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is what Roger Allam didn't attend, and the letters that spell it are in front of you. RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London; Allam, an actor heard often on Radio 4, trained at university instead.
explanation.definitionFit: RADA is the famous London drama school an actor like Allam might be expected to have attended.

clue.text: Start with the French on In Our Time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another comes above it

blocks.note: anno Domini, 'in the year of our Lord'

explanation.surface: Advice to open with French material on In Our Time, the Radio 4 history-of-ideas programme.
explanation.walkthrough: In Our Time looks like a programme title only; read as words it gives AD, the era of 'our Lord'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a lead is the start you have over the rest of the field.

clue.text: One drawn in by last two pieces in The Skewer, getting attention

indicators.note: one piece is pulled inside the others
the final two letters of the word

blocks.clueFragment: last two pieces in The Skewer
blocks.note: the final two letters of Skewer

explanation.surface: Something catching the attention of readers of The Skewer, Jon Holmes's satirical Radio 4 show.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside ER. To have someone's ear is to have their attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear means attention, as in 'lend me your ear'.

clue.text: Vehicle’s comics; genial Evans at centre

indicators.note: take the middle letters of each word

blocks.note: the middle two letters of COMICS
the middle two letters of GENIAL
the middle three letters of EVANS

explanation.surface: A line about comedians, with a friendly Evans at the heart of the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At centre' works on all three words before it, not just Evans: the middle of comics, genial and Evans run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A minivan is a small van, a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Before concluding parts of episode, Reardon (Ed) got smart

indicators.note: the final letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: last letters of episode and Reardon

explanation.surface: Someone called Ed Reardon smartens up before the end of an episode.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Reardon's Week is a Radio 4 comedy about a grumpy writer, so '(Ed)' looks like part of his name rather than a piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen is to make yourself smart, so preened means got smart.

clue.text: Ceremony, ponderous pronouncement crashes pips regularly

indicators.note: one piece crashes into the other, ending up inside it
something done regularly happens at even intervals, so letters are taken at even intervals: every other one

blocks.note: first and third letters of PIPS
the sacred syllable chanted in meditation

explanation.surface: A solemn announcement cuts across the pips, the Radio 4 time signal.
explanation.walkthrough: The pips are the six beeps that mark the hour on BBC radio. OM is the slow, sacred syllable intoned in Hindu and Buddhist prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: pomp is the splendour of a grand ceremony, as in 'pomp and circumstance'.

clue.text: Crawling about salon with flour

indicators.note: the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone crawling about a hair salon covered in flour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' only joins the two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone crawling is on hands and knees, on all fours.

clue.text: Hosts, quietly bitter ones

blocks.note: piano, the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: Radio hosts who are privately resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: P for quietly is the musical abbreviation piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by job: the people who front radio and TV programmes are their hosts.

clue.text: Bloody bell sounded by Spooner lookalike

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: bloody = RED, which takes the D from DINGER
a bell is a DINGER, which takes the R from RED

explanation.surface: A gory bell sounds out, rung by the Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: A dinger is something that dings, so a bell. Swap the first sounds of RED DINGER and you get DEAD RINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is someone who looks exactly like someone else.

clue.text: Fish eaten by Martha Kearney

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: The Radio 4 presenter Martha Kearney has a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: Martha Kearney presents on Radio 4; the fish is inside her name, across the gap between her two names.
explanation.definitionFit: Hake is a sea fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Mum, child rattle container

blocks.note: to jar is to jolt or shake

explanation.surface: A mother, a child and a baby's rattle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads rattle as a baby's toy; as a verb it means jar.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason jar is a glass jar with a screw lid, used for preserving.

clue.text: See 20d
Herc’s head, aviation firm that’s slim

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Hercules transport plane leads an airline's fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: Herc is aviation slang for the Hercules transport plane, which makes 'aviation firm' look like its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline crack or gap is very thin, as slim as a hair.

clue.text: A politician greeting Webb finally promises – on the waves – to become grounded?

definitions.text: on the waves – to become grounded?

indicators.note: the final letter of the word

blocks.note: IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: An MP says hello to Justin Webb of Radio 4's Today programme and makes some promises.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a riddle: something that works on the waves and can then come ashore is amphibious.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphibious means able to work both on water and on land.

clue.text: Caught by Jake Yapp’s second character: rock out and amuse

indicators.note: the second letter of the word
letters out of place are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock fan is caught up in the comedian Jake Yapp's act and entertained.
explanation.walkthrough: Jake Yapp is a comedian on Radio 4; 'caught by' looks like a container but just adds C to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom used as a verb: telling a joke is a way to amuse a room.

clue.text: Marian welcomes Tara’s tip, one that’s out of this world

definitions.text: one that’s out of this world

indicators.note: the first word takes the other in
the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman named Marian takes a tip from Tara, whom she thinks is otherworldly.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside MARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martian comes from Mars, literally out of this world.

clue.text: Bohemian radio’s dead air

blocks.note: first definition: someone who has left conventional society
second definition: a moment when the signal cuts out

explanation.surface: An unconventional station broadcasts silence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs the two senses as one arty station; a signal dropout is a gap where the sound cuts out.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop-out is someone who rejects conventional society, like a bohemian; a dropout is also a sudden loss of signal.

clue.text: Intros to Loose Ends interrupting journalists: they rise in irritation

indicators.note: the introductions of words are their first letters
the letters break into the other word

blocks.note: hack is slang for a journalist
first letters of Loose and Ends

explanation.surface: Journalists are irritated when Loose Ends, the Radio 4 chat show, keeps cutting in.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose Ends is a Saturday evening Radio 4 chat show, and its italic title makes the words look like one name rather than a source of two first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Your hackles, the hairs on your neck, are said to rise when you are angry.

clue.text: Fry rank chicken?

definitions.note: the answer is Fry's first name, and Fry stands for the whole name

blocks.note: a step is a grade or rank

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to fry a chicken that has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: Fry and rank look like a cooking instruction and a smell; Fry is Stephen Fry, the broadcaster and comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen is Stephen Fry's first name.

clue.text: Fashionable panellist on the radio, one putting you in stitches?

indicators.note: what is heard on the radio is heard, not seen

blocks.note: a juror sits on a jury panel

explanation.surface: A trendy radio panellist has everyone in stitches laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: Being in stitches looks like laughing at a comedy panel; here the stitches are the ones a doctor puts in after an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who injures you may leave you needing stitches.

clue.text: Show what hapless crossword setter admitted

annotation.answer: I'M SORRY I HAVEN'T A CLUE

blocks.note: first definition: the Radio 4 panel game
second definition: a setter out of clues would confess exactly this

explanation.surface: A setter confesses to being stumped by their own crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue is a long-running Radio 4 comedy panel show; a setter who cannot write clues would have to say exactly that. The answer runs on into 12 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Radio 4 show is also a plain apology for lacking a clue.

clue.text: Mysteries arisen: bears with start of Things Fell Apart?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
the letters fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A question about why bears would be connected with Things Fall Apart, Chinua Achebe's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title is split in two: Things gives its first letter and Fell Apart tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a brain-teaser is a puzzle, and a mystery is something puzzling to be solved.

clue.text: Initially, Everyman’s trusting Claudia Hammond to make impression

indicators.note: take the initial letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Everyman's, trusting, Claudia, Hammond

explanation.surface: The setter hopes the Radio 4 psychology presenter Claudia Hammond will make a good impression.
explanation.walkthrough: Claudia Hammond presents All in the Mind on Radio 4.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave, cutting lines into metal or glass so they leave a lasting mark.

clue.text: Brian Aldridge, somewhat obsessive

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used

explanation.surface: A verdict on Brian Aldridge's personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Aldridge is a wealthy farmer in The Archers, Radio 4's long-running rural soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Anal, short for anal-retentive, means obsessively fussy.

clue.text: Award describing second letter from Soul Music producer

definitions.note: Music shares Soul Music, the Radio 4 series about songs, with the wordplay

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so one piece goes round the other
the second letter of the word

blocks.note: Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A producer of Soul Music, the Radio 4 series, receives an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE goes round O. The title Soul Music is split: Soul gives a letter and Music joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is an instrument, something that produces music.

clue.text: Powerful man alongside Nick Robinson at the start and end, dancing about?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, a dance; 'dancing about?' is a playful hint at it rather than an exact swap

indicators.note: N sits at both the start and the end of Nick Robinson, so either reading gives the same letter

blocks.note: King Charles, or Charles Atlas the bodybuilder
to can mean beside, as in 'shoulder to shoulder'

blocks.clueFragment: Nick Robinson at the start and end
blocks.note: the letter that begins Nick and ends Robinson

explanation.surface: A strong man stands beside Nick Robinson of Radio 4's Today programme, and the two start dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alongside' looks like a link word but supplies TO, a rare sense worth learning. Nick Robinson is a presenter on Today, Radio 4's morning news programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s dance, the sort of thing you dance about to.

clue.text: Woman’s Hour, yes, covered one who laughs

indicators.note: the first letters are the cover laid over the answer

blocks.note: first letters of Hour and yes

explanation.surface: A moment of laughter on Woman's Hour, the Radio 4 magazine programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title Woman's Hour is split: Woman is the definition and Hour gives a letter. Ena is a crossword regular, from Ena Sharples of the TV soap Coronation Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Ena is a woman's name, a crossword regular.

clue.text: Check third character in Just One Thing’s heading off

indicators.note: the third letter of the word
the first letter is taken off

blocks.note: one thing = ITEM, losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A reminder to check the opening of Just One Thing, Michael Mosley's Radio 4 health series.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title Just One Thing is split across the wordplay: Just gives a letter, and one thing is an ITEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stemming bleeding or a tide of complaints means stopping or holding it back.

clue.text: Artist had yarn with owl, taking part in Ramblings

indicators.note: the letters ramble about into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist chats with an owl on Ramblings, Clare Balding's Radio 4 walking programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramblings looks like a programme title only; as a word it tells you the letters wander.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Warhol, the pop artist of the soup cans, is one artist among many.
